QUIC crypto tests for RFC9001 secrets, key derivation, packet encryption, decryption, and nonce generation.

# Purpose
This C file is a test program for QUIC initial packet crypto. It uses RFC 9001 test vectors and binary fixtures to verify `fd_quic_gen_initial_secrets`, `fd_quic_gen_keys`, `fd_quic_crypto_encrypt`, `fd_quic_crypto_decrypt_hdr`, `fd_quic_crypto_decrypt`, and `fd_quic_get_nonce`. The file defines expected client and server secrets, keys, IVs, and header protection keys, then checks that the library produces the same values from the destination connection ID `test_dst_conn_id`.

The [`main`](<#main>) function builds a full client Initial packet, encrypts it, compares the result with the fixture `test_client_encrypted`, and then decrypts the header and payload to confirm that the original packet is recovered. It also checks error cases for invalid sizes and offsets, tests short packet number handling, and verifies nonce generation against an RFC example. The file ends with simple throughput benchmarks for header and payload encrypt and decrypt paths, so it serves both as a correctness test and a performance check for QUIC crypto code.
